name: python-patterns
description: Context-driven Python development: frameworks, async, typing, structure.
allowed-tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep

ASK user for framework preference when unclear
Choose async vs sync based on CONTEXT
Don't default to same framework every time

Choose FastAPI for APIs/microservices or AI/ML serving; Django for full-stack, CMS, or admin; Flask for simple projects, scripts, or learning. Ask whether the project is API-only or full-stack, needs admin, and whether the team knows async.

Use async for I/O-bound work, concurrent connections, and real-time features; sync for CPU-bound work or blocking libraries. CPU work can use multiprocessing. Avoid mixing sync and async carelessly or using sync libraries in async code. Async options include httpx, redis-py async, SQLAlchemy 2.0 async, and Tortoise. In FastAPI, use async def with async database drivers or HTTP calls; use def with sync drivers or CPU work. Django async suits external calls and high-concurrency views; its async ORM is limited.

Type public APIs; let local types infer. Use Pydantic for API validation and request/response models. Organize by feature or layer: routes/, services/, models/, schemas/, dependencies/. Keep business logic out of routes. In Django, favor thin views, managers for common queries, select_related() for FKs, and prefetch_related() for M2M. Use dependencies for auth, testability, and cleanup.

For background work, consider BackgroundTasks for simple in-process tasks; Celery for distributed workflows; ARQ, RQ, or Dramatiq for queue-based alternatives. Raise domain exceptions in services; transform them in handlers. Return consistent error codes, messages, and relevant details; do not expose stack traces.

Test critical paths: unit tests with pytest, API integration with pytest + httpx/TestClient, and E2E workflows with pytest + DB. Choose the framework for this context; decide async strategy, typing, structure, error handling, and background-task needs.
